clue.text: Fruit shelter used to make an acceptable port

parts.note: a dark berry from a tree whose leaves feed silkworms
to harbour is to shelter, and a harbour is a sheltered place

explanation.surface: A fruit-storage shed somehow turned into a passable seaport.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mulberry harbours were prefabricated floating harbours towed across the Channel for the D-Day landings in 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: These temporary prefabricated harbours served the Allied invasion as a workable substitute for a captured real port.

clue.text: Service at foreign port ending in carnage

parts.note: the Mass is a church service
Acre is a port in Israel

explanation.surface: A church service in an overseas harbour town ends in bloodshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words denote the indiscriminate slaughter of many people at once.

clue.text: Instructor taking lead in foreign tour

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged
the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A teacher heads a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher who gives individual instruction to pupils.

clue.text: Creature that played Scottish music outside hostelry

indicators.note: outside tells us one piece wraps around the other on both sides

parts.note: first part of PIPED, played the bagpipes

explanation.surface: An animal that played the bagpipes outside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PIPED (played the bagpipes, the Scottish instrument) goes round INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinnipeds are seals, sea lions and walruses, so the word names a kind of animal.

clue.text: She advises, for example, where river rises

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Aire is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A female counsellor points to the source of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Egeria was the nymph who advised the Roman king Numa, so her name now means a female adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: An egeria is a woman who acts as a counsellor or mentor, after the nymph advising King Numa.

clue.text: Comprehends how company politician makes progress

explanation.surface: Explains how an MP climbs the ladder in a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprehend in the older sense is to include or contain, which is what comprises means.

clue.text: Stars seen by soldier outside working mine

indicators.note: outside says one piece encloses the other
a thing being worked is being reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: first letter of GI, an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier near a working mine glimpses stars overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is a constellation and so a group of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Excessive verbiage not unusual to new part of London

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: padding is surplus words filling out a text

explanation.surface: Wordy waffle is not unusual for a newcomer to London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not unusual' reads as a phrase meaning common, but 'unusual' works alone on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Green is a district of west London, known for its police station.

clue.text: Dull girl lost in thought

parts.note: musing is pondering, deep in thought

explanation.surface: A boring young woman is miles away, lost in her own thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unamusing fails to entertain, so it is tedious and lacking interest.

clue.text: Conclusion of love article about girl

indicators.note: about means around, so the pair of letters goes round the name

explanation.surface: How a love letter ends, with a word about a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: O and A together go around MEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end or final part of anything.

clue.text: Fool taking round gift of an instrument

indicators.note: taking something round means wrapping one part around another

parts.note: first letter of BOON, a gift or blessing

explanation.surface: An idiot carries round a present of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking round' looks as if the fool takes the gift, but it is the gift that goes round the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a large double-reed woodwind of the orchestra.

clue.text: Answered traveller and didn't tell the truth

explanation.surface: A salesman gave an answer and it was a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply is to respond, so the past tense matches answered.

clue.text: Right one to stock

parts.note: an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: The correct item to keep on the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' tempts as a verb about shopkeeping; here it is the noun for lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock in the sense of ancestry or descent means the same as race or breed.

clue.text: Phantom pair in a top review

indicators.note: to review is to go over and rework, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A ghostly couple star in a first-rate theatrical revue.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition is a ghost or spectre seen by the living.

clue.text: Coming upon flower by chance

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Stumbling across a bloom quite by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, the thing that flows. 'By chance' looks like a phrase; only 'chance' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense an adventure is a hazard or chance event, something that happens by luck.

clue.text: Produced something and gave up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gave a crop or return

explanation.surface: Someone made an effort, then surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: A field yields a harvest, and an army yields to its enemy, two senses of one verb.

clue.text: Hinder public relations on occasion

explanation.surface: Publicity people get in the way at a function.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop or obstruct it from happening.

clue.text: High pointed rock seen as boat rounds headland

indicators.note: rounds means goes around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: start of PINNACE, a small ship's boat
read as head of land: the first letter of land

explanation.surface: A tall jagged crag comes into view as a boat sails round a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headland' reads as one word, a cape, but splits into head and land. A pinnace is a ship's tender.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a tall slender peak or spire of rock.

clue.text: Oriental boy holding drunkard's secret

indicators.note: holding means having something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: An Eastern lad keeps a drinker's confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: E and ERIC together hold SOT between them; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an inner circle, so it is hidden or private.

clue.text: Cleaning done by sailor on Regent Street mistakenly

indicators.note: done mistakenly means put in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: REGENT plus ST for street, rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman scrubbing the pavement of a famous London shopping street by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent Street is a major shopping street in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstergent is a rare word for something with a cleansing or purging effect, like a detergent.

clue.text: What athlete's have for stimulants?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the brief trousers runners wear
second meaning: small measures of spirits, pick-me-ups

explanation.surface: What do athletes take as performance enhancers?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at doping; the second sense is the British word for a nip of spirits served in a small measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners wear short trousers, and small glasses of whisky or gin are drinks that perk you up.

clue.text: Fish you obtain when vessel comes in

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: The catch you land when your boat comes into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat in the surface; here it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The gurnet, or gurnard, is a spiny sea fish with a large armoured head.

clue.text: Low hill

definitions.meaning: first meaning: depressed, in low spirits
second meaning: a rolling chalk upland

explanation.walkthrough: 'Low hill' reads as one phrase, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling dejected is being down, and a down is a grassy upland such as the English South Downs.

clue.text: Girl goes into mother with delicious food

indicators.note: going into means entering, so one piece is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: A daughter joins her mum to share a tasty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the food from heaven in Exodus, so it stands for any delightful sustenance.

clue.text: Fish put by novice in hat

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: first part B of BOATER, a flat straw hat

explanation.surface: A fish placed by a beginner inside a straw hat.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside BOATER, after its first letter. A boater is a stiff flat-crowned straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a herring that has been salted and lightly smoked whole.

clue.text: Inexpert morning article true to form

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unskilled morning newspaper piece runs exactly to type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True to form' is a stock phrase; split it, and 'form' alone works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur work is unprofessional and lacking skill, so the adjective means inexpert.

clue.text: Pronounce complete

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to speak or say

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the adjective look like an instruction; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to say aloud, the other the adjective meaning total or absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: For example, worker in row at plant

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: first letter of LINE, a row

explanation.surface: A labourer in a line of men at the factory, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory in the surface; here it is a botanical plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose with fragrant leaves, so it is a plant.
